title: Benchmarking Uncertainty Calibration in Large Language Model Long-Form Question Answering

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the aggregated probability mass assigned to each multiple-choice label (e.g., A, B, C, D) across datasets against the ground truth distribution to identify systematic model preferences for specific answers regardless of semantic content.
Evaluating systematic preferences for certain label positions in multiple-choice formats, which the researchers isolate and mitigate using the APriCoT counterfactual prompting strategy.

Analyzing the distribution of confidence scores assigned by methods like P(True) and Verbalized Uncertainty to identify overwhelming polarization, such as a model's tendency to default to near 1.0 confidence scores irrespective of actual accuracy.
